name: Honey and ginger throat soothing

lead: Honey and ginger in warm drinks are used to soothe a sore throat and keep the voice comfortable and easy to use.

Proponents say honey coats the throat and ginger soothes it. A Cochrane review cited on Wikipedia found no strong evidence for or against honey for coughs, while the WHO recommends honey for coughs and sore throats. Ginger has a long traditional-medicine history, and its effectiveness for treating disease remains uncertain.

paras: People stir honey, fresh ginger or both into hot water or tea, usually when the throat feels rough or after heavy voice use.
Honey should not be given to infants under one because of infant botulism risk. Ginger can interact with anticoagulants.

angle.text: Honey and ginger drinks soothe a sore, irritated throat so the voice feels easier and clearer. Honey has some cough data and WHO guidance for sore throats, while ginger rests on traditional use.

paras: Evidence for honey easing children's cough is described as moderate to low quality. The UK MHRA suggests honey and lemon as a safer option than OTC cough medicine for children under six. Honey is not recommended before age one because of infant botulism risk. [1]
Ginger may help pregnancy nausea per low-quality evidence; it can cause heartburn, may interact with anticoagulants, and large amounts may cause GI discomfort. [2]
No studies found on honey and ginger for voice or vocal strain specifically; honey studies cover cough in general. [1]
